priority_policy.P0: Blocks correctness, policy freshness, or release-grade diagnosis for the first supported RL integration.
priority_policy.P1: Blocks faithful replay of the broader RL lifecycle but not request-plane serving validation.
priority_policy.P2: Follow-on capability that must not delay the request-plane documentation foundation.

closed_loop_decision.owner_team: Dynamo RL, observability, planner, and simulation maintainers
closed_loop_decision.rationale: Keep capture, live replay, and DynoSim request-plane workflows in the current documentation goal. Do not assign or document a stable closed-loop RL simulator package until correlation, served-policy identity, update events, and lifecycle replay contracts are approved and validated.
acceptance_conditions: An approved DEP defines framework-owned versus Dynamo-owned event semantics.
A named package and maintenance owner accepts the deterministic packaging contract.
A prototype replays policy transitions, update pauses/failures, sample completion, and acceptance without moving reward or trainer semantics into Dynamo.
Repeated end-to-end live runs calibrate the simulator and disclose material error.
Security and retention review covers prompts, rewards, environment/tool results, and policy artifacts.

gaps.title: Typed RL correlation and freshness context
gaps.owner_team: Dynamo protocol, RL, router, and observability maintainers
gaps.problem: Dynamo can retain session identity, but it has no stable typed framework, job, rollout, sample, request-role, policy-version, trainer-step, or maximum-policy-lag context.
gaps.current_boundary: Frameworks must keep these values in their own ledger and may use explicitly allowlisted opaque headers for trace correlation. The router cannot enforce policy freshness from those headers.
gaps.desired_contract: Define an additive mixed-version-safe RL correlation envelope, propagation rules, cardinality/security constraints, and which fields are descriptive versus enforceable by routing.

contains: The current typed Dynamo request extension does not contain a stable RL policy version, target trainer step, or maximum lag field
No stable typed framework, rollout, sample, trainer-step, or policy-version fields

acceptance_evidence: Approved field semantics and ownership in a DEP.
Serialization, request propagation, trace capture, and N-2 mixed-version compatibility tests.
One framework adapter demonstrates end-to-end correlation without high-cardinality metric labels.
Security review defines trusted inputs, redaction, retention, and authorization boundaries.
Router tests distinguish descriptive policy identity from enforced maximum-lag behavior.
gaps.docs_behavior: Keep RL identity application-owned and describe opaque headers as correlation conventions, not shipped routing or validation fields.
gaps.expiration_trigger: A typed RL context or equivalent policy-freshness request contract lands.

gaps.title: Served policy-content identity
gaps.owner_team: Dynamo RL, protocol, vLLM, SGLang, and weight-lifecycle maintainers
gaps.problem: Current weight-version values are caller-supplied labels and request traces do not prove which immutable policy content served a response.
gaps.current_boundary: Validation must combine framework/update-control evidence, per-worker readback where available, cache handling, output mutation or numerical checks, and post-update generation. A version string alone is insufficient.
gaps.desired_contract: Define an immutable served-policy identity or attestation, its relationship to framework trainer steps and backend state, and how it is attached to request completion without hashing full weights on the serving path.

contains: Current request traces do not define standardized weight-update events or typed served-policy fields
Immutable served-policy identity or attestation joined to each completion

acceptance_evidence: Approved identity semantics that do not require full-weight hashing on every request.
Backend-specific update and readback tests map one immutable identity to every targeted worker.
Request completion evidence carries or joins to the verified served-policy identity.
Partial update, rollback, worker restart, and mixed-version failure tests prevent false attestation.
One framework run proves accepted-sample freshness using the served identity.
gaps.docs_behavior: Treat caller-supplied version text as an application/control-ledger correlation value and require independent update plus post-update evidence.
gaps.expiration_trigger: A released served-policy identity or content-attestation contract lands across a validated backend path.

gaps.title: Standard weight-update lifecycle events
gaps.owner_team: Dynamo RL, observability, vLLM, SGLang, and weight-lifecycle maintainers
gaps.problem: The request/operations trace has no standard event for gate, pause, transfer, cache reset, verification, failure, rollback, resume, or warm-up phases.
gaps.current_boundary: Framework and control services must preserve update timing and per-worker results separately, align clocks, and inspect request gaps and backend logs.
gaps.desired_contract: Emit bounded, backend-neutral update lifecycle events with update ID, target identity, worker role, phase, timestamps, result class, cache action, and safe error classification.

contains: The current request trace has no standardized weight-update event
Record update lifecycle in the framework/control-service ledger

acceptance_evidence: Schema and serialization tests cover every lifecycle phase and result class.
One colocated and one external/disaggregated update path emit complete per-worker timelines.
Partial failure and rollback/retry tests preserve one unambiguous terminal update result.
Trace overhead and cardinality measurements establish safe defaults.
Operations report or successor joins update events without exposing sensitive model paths or credentials.
gaps.docs_behavior: Keep the update timeline in the framework/control ledger and never infer success, atomicity, or duration from request gaps or a version label alone.
gaps.expiration_trigger: Standardized update lifecycle events ship and pass two-topology validation.

gaps.title: RL lifecycle replay event contract
gaps.owner_team: Dynamo RL, data-generation, replay, planner, and framework maintainers
gaps.problem: Current Dynamo replay consumes serving request shape and optional tool/session timing but not trainer phases, policy transitions, update pauses/failures, sample completion, acceptance, or reward outcomes.
gaps.current_boundary: Live replay and DynoSim can reproduce or model the captured request plane only. They cannot recompute framework decisions or training quality.
gaps.desired_contract: Define an optional framework-owned lifecycle event stream and deterministic lowering that preserves phase barriers, policy transitions, update windows, sample terminal states, and acceptance without moving reward or optimizer semantics into Dynamo.

contains: Optional framework-owned phase, transition, update-window, sample-terminal, and acceptance events with deterministic lowering

acceptance_evidence: Versioned event schema clearly separates framework-owned and Dynamo-owned semantics.
Deterministic safe fixture covers phase barriers, one policy transition, update failure, sample completion, and acceptance.
Capture-to-lowering count and ordering invariants pass under retries, cancellations, and incomplete samples.
Request-plane replay remains backward compatible when lifecycle events are absent.
One real framework trace replays timing/state transitions without claiming reward or optimizer recomputation.
gaps.docs_behavior: Describe live replay and DynoSim as request-plane tools and list trainer, reward, policy-transition, and acceptance behavior as omitted.
gaps.expiration_trigger: A versioned lifecycle event stream and deterministic replay lowering land.

gaps.title: Closed-loop RL simulator ownership and package
gaps.owner_team: Dynamo RL, planner, DynoSim, AI simulation, and framework maintainers
gaps.problem: There is no approved ownership, package, determinism, security, or calibration contract for simulating the trainer/reward/environment/policy loop together with Dynamo serving.
gaps.current_boundary: The current documentation stops at calibrated request-plane live replay and DynoSim. Full closed-loop RL simulation is a follow-on product/engineering decision.
gaps.desired_contract: Approve whether closed-loop capability extends DynoSim/AI simulation or uses a separate experimental package, with explicit semantic ownership, deterministic packaging, artifact security, fidelity metrics, and live calibration.

contains: Do not describe this workflow as full closed-loop RL simulation

acceptance_evidence: Approved DEP names the package, DRI, framework boundary, and long-term maintenance owner.
All prerequisite gap acceptance evidence is complete on at least one framework path.
Deterministic portable artifact executes the same closed-loop event graph repeatedly.
Live end-to-end calibration reports error for every decision metric and rejects material divergence.
Security review covers model/checkpoint, prompt, reward, tool/environment, and user-data artifacts.
gaps.docs_behavior: Keep closed-loop simulation out of the shipped RL documentation surface; document only request-plane fidelity and the follow-on decision boundary.
gaps.expiration_trigger: An approved closed-loop DEP assigns ownership and a validated experimental implementation lands.
